beliefs: Each character is shifted by +1 in Unicode code point [E1-E8]
Space is not special: it shifts to '!' like any other char [E2]
After shifting, a single 'Y' is inserted at index floor(len(s)/2) where len is code-point length [E1-E8]
If any character's code point is U+10FFFF, shifting +1 gives U+110000 which is invalid, so f raises ValueError and the whole call returns 'ERROR: ValueError' [E9]
U+10FFFE shifts fine to U+10FFFF (valid), only U+10FFFF itself triggers the error [E9]
The error is per-call: if any input in the probe contains U+10FFFF, that input's output is 'ERROR: ValueError' [E9]?
notes: Added handling for the U+10FFFF overflow: shifting produces U+110000 which is invalid, so the box raises ValueError and reports 'ERROR: ValueError' for that input. Other inputs in the same probe still compute normally.
